original_question: Decide whether elementary particles admit a quantum-liquid description that can predict particle masses, whether isolated quarks or hypothetical more fundamental constituents called rishons can exist either in nature or in strong electromagnetic-field environments, and whether quarks or rishons can be explained from a version of quantum mechanics based on more than two truth values, from quantum mechanics formulated with quaternion numbers, or from the differential equation used for a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate, including how that condensate model would affect rotational dynamics of quarks and whether neutrino mass has a related quaternion-type symmetry.
target_in_paper: Section 1.1, Problems in elementary particles etc., specifically the list introduced by the sentence "Now from these 'known' questions, we can also ask some new questions for further development of theoretical physics," items (i), (ii), (iii), (v), (vi), (vii), and (viii) on pp. 9-10.
correct_elements: Your draft is aimed at the correct part of the paper and captures, nearly item by item, seven of the subsection 1.1 open questions: a quantum-liquid model of elementary particles and mass prediction; isolated quarks or rishons in Nature; isolated quarks or rishons in strong electromagnetic fields; explanations of quarks/rishons via multivalued-logic Quantum Mechanics; explanations via Quaternion Quantum Mechanics; quaternion-type symmetry in neutrino mass; and an explanation via the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate together with the effect of the Magnus force on quark rotation.
missing_details: The paper does not present these as one single official conjecture or theorem; it presents them as separate open questions in a numbered list, and your draft merges them into one sentence.
Your draft omits the extra clause in item (vi): if Quaternion Quantum Mechanics explains quarks/rishons, the paper also asks how to ascribe physical meaning to a scalar in the quaternion field.

The paper's immediate context identifies rishons through Harari's preon-like model with two basic constituents, T and V, and gives their quark/lepton combinations; your draft only says they are hypothetical more fundamental constituents.
The paper separates the existence questions into two distinct cases: isolated quarks/rishons in Nature, and isolated quarks/rishons in a strong electromagnetic-field environment.

The neutrino clause in the paper is specifically about quaternion-type symmetry in neutrino mass, with Adler's QQM theory named as an example; that attribution is implicit in your draft rather than explicit.
The Gross-Pitaevskii part is conditional in the paper: if quarks/rishons can be explained from that viewpoint, then one should ask how the Magnus effect affects the rotational dynamics of quarks.
Section 1.1 does not specify what would count as a successful mass prediction, what observable would certify an isolated quark/rishon, or what level of theoretical explanation is intended.

Section 1.1 names multivalued-logic Quantum Mechanics, Quaternion Quantum Mechanics, and the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate, but it does not define their variables, operators, state spaces, or coupling to quarks/rishons.

No ambient ring or field, operator definition, homogeneity assumption, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic quantifier appears in the target passage; these are not part of the paper's formulation, except that item (vi) explicitly mentions the quaternion field.
refined_question: Could one (a) formulate a quantum-liquid model of elementary particles that predicts elementary-particle masses, and (b) determine whether quarks or Harari rishons can exist in isolation either in Nature or in a strong electromagnetic-field environment, and whether quarks/rishons admit a theoretical explanation from the viewpoints of multivalued-logic Quantum Mechanics, Quaternion Quantum Mechanics—including a physical interpretation of a scalar in the quaternion field and a possible quaternion-type symmetry of neutrino mass—or the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate, including the resulting Magnus-effect contribution to the rotational dynamics of quarks?
justification: The draft is not targeting a formal mathematical conjecture such as a Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; this paper is a compendium of open problems, and the wording of the draft matches the subsection 1.1 open-question list almost verbatim. In Section 1.1, pp. 9-10, the paper asks: (i) whether one can come up with a quantum liquid model of elementary particles and predict masses; (ii) whether isolated quarks or rishons can be found in Nature; (iii) whether isolated quarks or rishons can be found in a strong electromagnetic field environment; (v) whether quarks/rishons can be explained from multivalued-logic Quantum Mechanics; (vi) whether they can be explained from Quaternion Quantum Mechanics and, if so, how to ascribe physical meaning to a scalar in the quaternion field; (vii) whether neutrino mass has quaternion-type symmetry; and (viii) whether quarks/rishons can be explained from the Gross-Pitaevskii equation for a rotating Bose-Einstein condensate and, if so, how the Magnus effect affects quark rotational dynamics. The immediately preceding Harari paragraph in Section 1.1, pp. 8-9, supplies the paper's intended meaning of rishons. Later quaternion/Gross-Pitaevskii material in Section 7.4 (body heading printed as 6.4), pp. 80-82, gives additional background and an explicit Gross-Pitaevskii equation plus Conjecture 1, but that later section is not the official open-problem statement your draft is trying to capture.
